headline: Maersk ransom claim, Iran-linked arson case, and Enable Central hotfix dominate
overview: Today's core news shows lead with a Maersk data theft and ransom demand, a China-linked malware supplier link, and United Airlines blocking AI booking agents. The security patch cycle is also heavy: Apache, Fortinet, Ivanti, a Windows CLFS bypass, and the Enable Central hotfix. Several other shows add detail on Outlook, Barracuda, and Zen Orchestra exploitation, though some episode texts were thin or only partly available.

topStories.title: Maersk reports stolen data and a $5M ransom demand
topStories.summary: Maersk says attackers took about 100 GB from a local system at a company it acquired and are demanding $5 million in Bitcoin. The company reports no sign of impact on other systems or partners and expects no operational disruption, and the investigation is ongoing.

topStories.title: Patch wave: Apache, Fortinet, Ivanti, Windows CLFS and Enable Central
topStories.summary: Apache fixed a critical heap overflow in mod_http2 that could allow remote code execution, and Fortinet released 89 advisories with 17 rated critical. Ivanti patched an EPM SQL injection, and a public Windows CLFS escalation called SignDrop has no CVE or Microsoft confirmation yet. Enable released a hotfix for Central servers, and the number of exposed instances has dropped sharply.

topStories.title: China-linked campaigns may share a malware supplier
topStories.summary: Checkpoint Research links three China-linked hacking campaigns across Latin America, Asia and Europe to a possible shared malware supplier it calls Copper Dragon, based on code and infrastructure. The link to one campaign rests on infrastructure rather than matching code.

topStories.title: Iran-directed arson attacks streamed over FaceTime charged in US
topStories.summary: US prosecutors charged three men with directing attacks across Europe for Iran's Revolutionary Guard, including London arson attacks filmed for propaganda. Evidence came from stored files on a seized iPhone rather than from breaking FaceTime encryption, and the men face terrorism charges.

topStories.title: Outlook zero-day and exploited Barracuda and Zen Orchestra flaws
topStories.summary: Attackers are using an Outlook flaw that leaks password hashes when a crafted message file is opened, and Microsoft's Office update addresses it. Barracuda email gateway flaws are being exploited, and a login bypass in Zen Orchestra lets attackers sign in as admin and reach root on hosts.

topStories.title: Anthropic IPO and the wider AI market
topStories.summary: Anthropic is reportedly seeking a valuation between roughly $1.25 and $1.4 trillion ahead of a planned IPO, with reports of possibly higher pricing given demand. Its new productivity suite competes with Microsoft tools. Separately, Google released Gemini 4 Carbon and the Nvidia smuggling scandal continues.

episodes.title: Maersk gets a $5M ransom note, CopperDragon's malware connections, United grounds AI booking bots
episodes.summary: Covers the Maersk data theft and ransom demand, Copper Dragon malware links, United blocking AI booking bots, the Chilean administrator identification, Zoom Windows patches, the Iran-linked FaceTime arson case, the Enable Central fix, and Anti-Fox links to AWS intrusions. One sponsor segment was ignored.

episodes.title: SANS Stormcast Thursday, November 12th, 2026: Apache mod_http2 RCE (CVE-2026-119618); Fortinet FortiMail Criticals; Ivanti EPM SQLi (CVE-2026-121653); Windows SignDrop CLFS; N-able N-central HF2
episodes.summary: Covers the Apache mod_http2 heap overflow, the Fortinet advisories, the Ivanti EPM SQL injection, the SignDrop Windows CLFS escalation with public proof of concept, and the Enable Central hotfix with reduced exposure.

episodes.title: Wall Street Has No Idea What Anthropic Is Worth
episodes.summary: Covers the Gemini 4 Carbon release, the Nvidia China smuggling scandal, OpenAI's revenue and travel acquisition, and Anthropic's IPO pricing, compute commitments and productivity suite launch. Sponsor segments were ignored.

episodes.title: How hackers turned Russian cars into pumpkins
episodes.summary: Text is a partial transcript with a rambling intro and an extended sponsor segment. It discusses deepfake-driven scams and a hacking story about Russian cars, but the coverage is too partial to summarise in detail.

episodes.title: Claude Chat Invites and a Backdoored Coding Extension
episodes.summary: Covers two initial access campaigns that abused Claude: chat-sharing notifications used as callback phishing lures, and a tampered Claude Code extension in a marketplace that installed an SSH backdoor. Includes hunting and reimaging advice.

episodes.title: Outlook zero-day, Barracuda gateway exploited, Xen Orchestra bypass | Cyber Security News Nov 11
episodes.summary: Covers the Outlook hash-leak flaw, Barracuda gateway exploitation, the Zen Orchestra login bypass, the Enable Central hotfix, SAP maximum-severity flaws, Turla's Serial tool, a malicious Git repository issue, and several AI and iOS items.

episodes.title: 🚨 SAP 4 CVSS 10.0 Flaws: ICM2Shell & ProxyGate, N-Able Offline After 30 Zero-Days, 8th Chrome 0-Day
episodes.summary: Episode description lists SAP flaws, the Enable Central offline advice, and a Chrome zero-day, plus a Barracuda gateway story and Patch Tuesday. The show notes contain mainly promotional and link text, so the detail is limited.

episodes.title: Local Chinese Model Seeks Nvidia Hardware – 2026-11-09
episodes.summary: The transcript is mostly casual chat about cars and an off-topic discussion, with no specific security news clearly covered.
